Ui.Script:
BENILLA_LOOT_NUMBUTTONS = 4
-- The 1.12 item-quality palette — now the shared ITEM_QUALITY_COLORS global (Fonts.xml, -- its home since the unit popup became a second customer); the local name kept for this -- file's existing readers. Indexed 0..6; an unknown/nil quality falls back to common. BENILLA_LOOT_QUALITY_COLORS = ITEM_QUALITY_COLORS
local function loot_color(quality) return BENILLA_LOOT_QUALITY_COLORS[quality] or BENILLA_LOOT_QUALITY_COLORS[1] end
function BenillaLootItem_OnLoad(button, index) button.lootButton = index button.icon = getglobal(button:GetName() .. "Icon") button.name = getglobal(button:GetName() .. "Name") button.count = getglobal(button:GetName() .. "Count") -- Left-click loots the row (the C LootButton behaviour, LootFrame.lua l.94/147). button:RegisterForClicks("LeftButtonUp", "RightButtonUp") end
-- ref LootFrameItem_OnClick (LootFrame.lua l.147-162): CTRL previews the row's item in the -- dressing room (decision 1060), SHIFT posts its link into an open chat edit box (decision -- 1059) — both through GetLootSlotLink, the row-link binding this arc added (loot.rs). -- -- WHERE THE TAKE LIVES, and why the gate below reads three modifiers where FrameXML names -- two (VERIFIED at the 1.12.1 bytes — wow-re `ui/scratch/loot-click-modifier-gate.md`, -- decision 1067). The reference's Lua handler suppresses NOTHING, because the take is the C -- `CLootButton`'s own click behaviour (`LootFrame.lua:94`'s `button:SetSlot(slot)` hands the -- widget the slot). `CLootButton::OnClick 0x4c1820` runs the Lua `<OnClick>` FIRST and -- unconditionally, then gates itself on `0x41f8f0(0/1/2)` — byte-identically the predicates -- behind `IsShiftKeyDown`/`IsControlKeyDown`/**`IsAltKeyDown`** — and only then sends -- (`0x4c2790` → `0x5e1ad0` → `push 0x108`, CMSG_AUTOSTORE_LOOT_ITEM). -- -- Three consequences, all of them this handler's shape: -- · **ALT suppresses the take too**, though no FrameXML file mentions alt. Its gate is C. -- · The gate is on ANY modifier being HELD, not on "the arm that handled it": a shift-click -- with the chat box closed does nothing in Lua and still must not loot. -- · The button code is never read (`0x4c1820` doesn't look at it), so a RIGHT-click loots -- exactly like a left one — which is why this handler takes no `mouseButton`. -- -- benilla folds that C action into this Lua handler (`LootSlot(button.slot)`, this file's -- model since 0084), so the gate has to be an early return here. Named divergence, not a -- transcription slip: 1.12 exposes no plain "take slot N" binding at all — the real -- `LootSlot 0x4c2e70` is the LOOT_BIND *confirmation continuation* (flag 1, gated on the -- stashed slot at `[0x847cec]`; its only FrameXML caller is `StaticPopup.lua:606`). Moving -- the take host-side onto the widget, and shrinking `LootSlot()` to that continuation, is -- 1067's named follow-up. -- -- The reference's tail (StaticPopup_Hide("CONFIRM_LOOT_DISTRIBUTION") and the four -- LootFrame.selected* fields, l.155-161) is the MASTER-LOOT dropdown's bookkeeping — -- GroupLootDropDown reads exactly those four (l.164+). benilla ships no master loot -- (benilla-protocol's loot module: CMSG_LOOT_MASTER_GIVE/SMSG_LOOT_MASTER_LIST out of -- scope), so returning early skips nothing that exists. -- -- The coin row has no link (it is synthesized, with no item behind it — ui_loot.rs), so a -- modified click on it finds nil: DressUpItemLink returns on a nil link (DressUpFrame.lua -- l.10-16) and the insert is skipped. It does not fall through to looting the money either, -- which is the same law the item rows follow. function BenillaLootItem_OnClick(button) -- The row remembers its resolved loot slot from the last Update; act on it (LootFrame.lua -- l.94-95 stores button.slot, the click calls LootSlot on it). if not button.slot then return end if IsControlKeyDown() then DressUpItemLink(GetLootSlotLink(button.slot)) -- ref l.148-149 return elseif IsShiftKeyDown() then -- ref l.150-153, through the shared helper (UIParent.xml): it carries the ref's own -- "only when the edit box is up" guard AND our nil-link one, which this row needs -- more than most — the coin row never has a link, and an item row has none until -- its template lands. A shift-click with chat closed does nothing here: a loot row -- has no stack to split, unlike a bag slot. BenillaChatEdit_InsertLink(GetLootSlotLink(button.slot)) return elseif IsAltKeyDown() then -- The C gate's third modifier (`0x41f8f0(2)` @ `0x4c1841`). Nothing is bound to -- alt in FrameXML, so this arm does nothing at all — its entire job is to NOT -- loot, which is what the real client does and what we did not. return end LootSlot(button.slot) end
-- Hover: the item name coloured by quality (loot rows carry it — GetLootSlotInfo's 4th -- return), reusing loot_color. The coin pile has no item quality; its formatted text (already -- the row name) shows white. function BenillaLootItem_OnEnter(button) if not button.slot then return end local texture, item, quantity, quality, itemId = GetLootSlotInfo(button.slot) button.itemId = itemId if not item then return end -- Snap beside the ICON, not the 160-wide row's far edge (the vendor rows' own idiom — -- MerchantFrame.xml walks ANCHOR_RIGHT back by a negative x): 37px icon on a 160 row -- → -123 lands the tip at the icon's right edge. GameTooltip:SetOwner(button, "ANCHOR_RIGHT", -123, 0) -- The shared item tooltip when the row is an ITEM (coin rows have no item id/stats). local color = loot_color(quality) if button.itemId and button.itemId ~= 0 then GameTooltip:SetItemById(button.itemId, item, quality) else GameTooltip:SetText(item, color.r, color.g, color.b) end if (quantity or 1) > 1 then GameTooltip:AddLine("Stack Size: " .. quantity, 1, 1, 1) end GameTooltip:Show() end
function BenillaLootItem_OnLeave(button) GameTooltip:Hide() end
-- LootFrame_Update (LootFrame.lua l.67-119): fill the visible rows for the current page. function BenillaLootFrame_Update() local frame = getglobal("BenillaLootFrame") local numItems = GetNumLootItems() -- Rows per page: 4, or 3 when there's a pager to make room for (l.70-73). local perPage = BENILLA_LOOT_NUMBUTTONS if numItems > BENILLA_LOOT_NUMBUTTONS then perPage = perPage - 1 end -- Clamp the page (a shrunk loot can leave us past the end — benilla's replacement for -- Blizzard's per-button collapse, l.38-50). local maxPage = 1 if numItems > 0 then maxPage = math.ceil(numItems / perPage) end if frame.page > maxPage then frame.page = maxPage end if frame.page < 1 then frame.page = 1 end
for index = 1, BENILLA_LOOT_NUMBUTTONS do local button = getglobal("BenillaLootButton" .. index) local slot = (perPage * (frame.page - 1)) + index if slot <= numItems and index <= perPage and (LootSlotIsItem(slot) or LootSlotIsCoin(slot)) then local texture, item, quantity, quality, itemId = GetLootSlotInfo(slot) button.icon:SetTexture(texture or BENILLA_FALLBACK_ICON) button.name:SetText(item or "...") local color = loot_color(quality) button.name:SetVertexColor(color.r, color.g, color.b) -- "xN" stack count only when more than one drops (LootFrame.lua l.87-93). if (quantity or 1) > 1 then button.count:SetText(quantity) else button.count:SetText("") end button.slot = slot button.itemId = itemId button:Show() else button:Hide() end end
-- Pager visibility (LootFrame.lua l.105-118): Up when past page 1, Down when more remain. if frame.page > 1 then getglobal("BenillaLootUpButton"):Show() else getglobal("BenillaLootUpButton"):Hide() end if frame.page < maxPage then getglobal("BenillaLootDownButton"):Show() else getglobal("BenillaLootDownButton"):Hide() end end
function BenillaLootFrame_PageDown() local frame = getglobal("BenillaLootFrame") frame.page = frame.page + 1 BenillaLootFrame_Update() end
function BenillaLootFrame_PageUp() local frame = getglobal("BenillaLootFrame") frame.page = frame.page - 1 BenillaLootFrame_Update() end
function BenillaLootFrame_OnLoad(frame) frame.page = 1 frame:RegisterEvent("LOOT_OPENED") frame:RegisterEvent("LOOT_UPDATE") frame:RegisterEvent("LOOT_CLOSED") end
function BenillaLootFrame_OnEvent(frame) if event == "LOOT_OPENED" then -- A fresh loot: reset to page 1, paint, show (LootFrame.lua l.14-16). frame.page = 1 BenillaLootFrame_Update() ShowUIPanel(frame) elseif event == "LOOT_UPDATE" then -- A content change while open (name/quality landed, a row/coin removed): repaint, -- keeping the current page. BenillaLootFrame_Update() elseif event == "LOOT_CLOSED" then HideUIPanel(frame) end end
function BenillaLootFrame_OnShow() -- Open sound — the window-sound convention (decision 0090), wrapper form (this handler -- has real logic beyond the sound, so it can't be a bare inline PlaySound). -- (LootFrame.lua LootFrame_OnShow, l.131-141). ONLY the empty-roll fork is -- Lua-side: an empty loot plays LOOTWINDOWOPENEMPTY (l.135-136). The normal (non-empty) -- loot-open sound is C-side (the server-driven loot handler), so we stay silent for it — -- there is no kit to guess. The fishing fork (l.137-139, "FISHING REEL IN" + the -- FishingLoot-Icon portrait swap) is omitted: benilla ships no fishing feed. (DR 0086: -- vmangos masks the lootable flag for empty rolls, so a live empty window is rare — but -- the branch must exist.) if GetNumLootItems() == 0 then PlaySound("LOOTWINDOWOPENEMPTY") end end
function BenillaLootFrame_OnHide() -- Closing the window releases the loot (LootFrame.lua l.143-145). The app only sends the -- release when a loot is actually open, so a hide after the state already cleared is a -- harmless no-op. No close sound here: LootFrame_OnHide plays none (the loot-close kit is -- C-side), so we stay silent — no kit to guess. CloseLoot() end
function BenillaLootCloseButton_OnClick() -- Hide immediately (client-authoritative); OnHide's CloseLoot() sends the release. HideUIPanel(getglobal("BenillaLootFrame")) end
